body.en: Advanced ACT Math requires fluency across multi-variable linear and non-linear systems, matrix algebraic structures, polynomial factor theorems, and logarithmic equations requiring extraneous root verification.

label.en: Definition 2.1 — Matrix Arithmetic, Determinants, and Inverses

body.en:
Matrix conventions for standardized mathematics examinations:
  • Matrix Addition and Scalar Multiplication: Defined entrywise for matrices of identical dimensions \(m \times n\).
  • Matrix Product (\(AB\)): The product \(A_{m \times k} B_{k \times n}\) produces an \(m \times n\) matrix where entry \((i, j)\) is the dot product of row \(i\) of \(A\) and column \(j\) of \(B\). Matrix multiplication is non-commutative: \(AB \neq BA\) in general.
  • \(2 \times 2\) Determinant & Inverse: For \(A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}\):
    \[ \det(A) = |A| = ad - bc \]\[ A^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad - bc} \begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix} \quad (\text{provided } \det(A) \neq 0) \]
  • Multiplicative Determinant Property: For square matrices \(A\) and \(B\), \(\det(AB) = \det(A) \cdot \det(B)\).

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Advanced Algebra & Systems

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across ACT International Subject Test — Math 1, multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

label.en: Theorem 2.1 — Polynomial Theorems and Logarithmic Properties

body.en:
High-rigor algebraic principles:
  • Polynomial Remainder & Factor Theorems: When a polynomial \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - c\), the remainder is \(R = P(c)\). Consequently, \((x - c)\) is a factor of \(P(x)\) if and only if \(P(c) = 0\).
  • Rational Root Theorem: Any rational root of \(a_n x^n + \dots + a_1 x + a_0 = 0\) with integer coefficients has the form \(\pm \frac{p}{q}\), where \(p\) divides \(a_0\) and \(q\) divides \(a_n\).
  • Logarithm Laws:
    \[ \log_b(xy) = \log_b x + \log_b y, \quad \log_b(x/y) = \log_b x - \log_b y, \quad \log_b(x^k) = k\log_b x \]
  • Extraneous Root Principle: Because \(\log_b(u)\) requires \(u > 0\) and \(\sqrt{u}\) requires \(u \ge 0\), solving converted polynomial forms may introduce extraneous roots that must be checked against the original expressions.

label.en: ▲ ACT Math 2 Traps & Pitfalls — Matrices & Advanced Systems

body.en:
• Matrix Multiplication Order & Dimensions: To compute \(AB\), the number of columns in \(A\) (inner dimension) must equal the number of rows in \(B\): \((m imes k) imes (k imes n) = (m imes n)\). Furthermore, \(AB eq BA\) in general — matrix multiplication is non-commutative!
  • Determinant & Singularity: For \(A = egin{pmatrix} a & b \ c & d \end{pmatrix}\), \(\det(A) = ad - bc\). The matrix inverse \(A^{-1}\) exists if and only if \(\det(A) eq 0\). If \(\det(A) = 0\), the corresponding linear system has either no unique solution (inconsistent or dependent).
  • Extraneous Solutions in Rational Equations: When clearing denominators by multiplying by a common multiple, values that make any original denominator equal to zero are extraneous and must be discarded.
  • Logarithm Bases & Power Properties: Remember \(\log_b(A + B) eq \log_b A + \log_b B\). The addition rule applies only inside the logarithm: \(\log_b(AB) = \log_b A + \log_b B\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Advanced Algebra & Systems)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

Find all intersection points of the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 25\) and the line \(x - y = 1\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Isolate \(x\) in the linear equation: \(x = y + 1\).
  2. Substitute into the circle equation:
    \[ (y + 1)^2 + y^2 = 25 \implies (y^2 + 2y + 1) + y^2 = 25 \]\[ 2y^2 + 2y - 24 = 0 \implies y^2 + y - 12 = 0 \]
  3. Factor the quadratic:
    \[ (y + 4)(y - 3) = 0 \implies y = 3 \quad \text{or} \quad y = -4 \]
  4. Determine corresponding \(x\)-values using \(x = y + 1\):
    If \(y = 3\): \(x = 3 + 1 = 4\), yielding \((4, 3)\).
    If \(y = -4\): \(x = -4 + 1 = -3\), yielding \((-3, -4)\).
  5. Verify in both equations:
    \(4^2 + 3^2 = 16 + 9 = 25\) and \(4 - 3 = 1\).
    \((-3)^2 + (-4)^2 = 9 + 16 = 25\) and \(-3 - (-4) = 1\).
The two intersection points are \(\mathbf{(4, 3)}\) and \(\mathbf{(-3, -4)}\).

label.en: Worked Example 2.B — Solving a Logarithmic Equation with Extraneous Roots

body.en:
Solve the equation \(\log_2(x + 3) + \log_2(x - 1) = 5\) for real \(x\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Combine terms using the product rule \(\log_b A + \log_b B = \log_b(AB)\):
    \[ \log_2[(x + 3)(x - 1)] = 5 \]
  2. Convert to exponential form:
    \[ (x + 3)(x - 1) = 2^5 = 32 \]
  3. Expand and set to zero:
    \[ x^2 + 2x - 3 = 32 \implies x^2 + 2x - 35 = 0 \]
  4. Factor the quadratic:
    \[ (x + 7)(x - 5) = 0 \implies x = 5 \quad \text{or} \quad x = -7 \]
  5. Verify against domain restrictions (\(x + 3 > 0 \implies x > -3\) and \(x - 1 > 0 \implies x > 1\)):
    For \(x = -7\): \(\log_2(-4)\) is undefined in real numbers (extraneous).
    For \(x = 5\): \(\log_2(8) + \log_2(4) = 3 + 2 = 5\) (valid).
The unique real solution is \(\mathbf{x = 5}\).

label.en: Worked Example \(C\) — Advanced Algebra & Systems (Hard Application)

body.en:
Problem (Hard): In the plane, the line \( 10u + 24y = 240 \) intersects the axes at points \( X \) and \( Y \). What is the sum of intercepts \( h \) of \( 10u + 24y = 240 \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: The intercepts are \( 24 \) and \( 10 \), whose sum is \( 24 + 10 = 34 \).

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Advanced Algebra & Systems (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): The ordered pair \( (u, y) \) satisfies \( u + y = 13 \) and \( 15u + 6y = 96 \). What is the coordinate \( u \) in \( h(u, y) \)?

Step-by-Step Solution: Substituting \( y = 13 - u \) into \( 15u + 6y = 96 \) yields \( u = 2 \).

Time spent at the slower speed is longer than time spent at the faster speed.

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Advanced Algebra & Systems

body.en: High-Speed Exam Shortcut (ACT International Subject Test — Math 1): When a linear system asks for a combined expression like \(3x + 3y\) rather than \(x\) and \(y\) individually, add or subtract the two equations directly before isolating either variable—this often yields the target expression in a single step.

question.en: Solve for \(x\): \(3^{x+1} = 5^x\). Express your solution in terms of natural logarithms.

solution.en:
Take the natural logarithm \(\ln\) of both sides:
\[ \ln(3^{x+1}) = \ln(5^x) \implies (x + 1)\ln 3 = x\ln 5 \]\[ x\ln 3 + \ln 3 = x\ln 5 \implies \ln 3 = x\ln 5 - x\ln 3 = x(\ln 5 - \ln 3) \]\[ x = \frac{\ln 3}{\ln 5 - \ln 3} = \mathbf{\frac{\ln 3}{\ln(5/3)}} \approx 2.151 \]

Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(\ln\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: When the polynomial \(P(x) = 2x^3 - kx^2 + 5x - 6\) is divided by \(x - 2\), the remainder is \(8\). What is the value of the constant \(k\)?

solution.en:
By the Polynomial Remainder Theorem, the remainder upon division by \(x - 2\) is equal to \(P(2)\):
\[ P(2) = 8 \]\[ 2(2^3) - k(2^2) + 5(2) - 6 = 8 \]\[ 2(8) - 4k + 10 - 6 = 8 \implies 16 - 4k + 4 = 8 \implies 20 - 4k = 8 \]\[ -4k = -12 \implies k = \mathbf{3} \]

Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(x - 2\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: Find all real solutions to the rational equation \(\dfrac{x}{x-2} + \dfrac{1}{x+3} = \dfrac{5}{x^2+x-6}\).

solution.en:
Notice that the common denominator factors as \(x^2 + x - 6 = (x - 2)(x + 3)\).
Domain restrictions: \(x \neq 2\) and \(x \neq -3\).
Multiply both sides by \((x - 2)(x + 3)\):
\[ x(x + 3) + (x - 2) = 5 \implies x^2 + 3x + x - 2 = 5 \]\[ x^2 + 4x - 7 = 0 \]
Apply the quadratic formula with \(a = 1, b = 4, c = -7\):
\[ x = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{4^2 - 4(1)(-7)}}{2(1)} = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{16 + 28}}{2} = \frac{-4 \pm \sqrt{44}}{2} = \frac{-4 \pm 2\sqrt{11}}{2} = \mathbf{-2 \pm \sqrt{11}} \]
Neither solution equals \(2\) or \(-3\), so both solutions are valid.

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Advanced Algebra & Systems and start from \(\dfrac{x}{x-2} + \dfrac{1}{x+3} = \dfrac{5}{x^2+x-6}\).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(x^2 + x - 6 = (x - 2)(x + 3)\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.
